Method: five topic researchers (press/macro and Friday data, oil and weekend developments, movers, Tier 3 AI financing, this week's calendar), each capped at a fixed share of the session's 200-search budget, then an independent fact-checker per topic with its own cap re-searched the items. Article pages could not be opened in this sandbox (WebFetch DNS failures), so evidence is search-result titles, URLs and snippets. Where press numbers conflict with the state file, the state file wins (§4C): closes and moves come from data/macro_series.csv, data/raw/movers_2026-10-16.json and data/raw/claims_check_2026-10-19.json. items.check: The CNBC article itself did not surface. Secondary coverage dated 10-15 does: digitaltoday.co.kr says CNBC reported CoreWeave 5y CDS 'topped 1,140 basis points during the session and later stood at 1,088'. A Chinese-language report says 1,194.5bp intraday record. Reuters-based pieces say it 'blew past 1,100 bps', and a Reuters-based article cites an implied 5-year default probability of nearly 63%. Reuters, Tom Westbrook and Amanda Cooper, businessday.co.za/world/international-companies/2026-10-15-ai-credit-fears-push-tech-default-insurance-to-record-highs/ (2026-10-15). I found no source for Oracle at 282bp.

items.safe_wording: Midweek (Thursday 10-15), Reuters and CNBC reported that the cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt against default (its five-year credit default swaps) had risen above 1,000 basis points, which means paying more than $10 a year to insure $100 of its bonds. Reported peaks ranged from about 1,100 to 1,195.
